item.title: The real AI economy is being built by ordinary people — Rest of World
item.description:
Rest of World · September 14, 2026 · ~15 min · Directly readable

Rest of World profiles workers and small-business owners across Asia and Africa who are folding AI into ordinary economic life. A Lagos makeup entrepreneur uses free chatbots for hiring, pricing and marketing; a Bengaluru café owner uses paid tools for sales analysis, recipe costing, translation and internal workflows while reserving cooking and hospitality for people. Across the profiles, adoption is selective: users delegate tasks where memory, drafting or calculation help, but keep judgment, craft or customer relationships where automation would damage the point of the work.

Why it broadens: Shifts the AI-economy lens away from model makers, venture funding and aggregate productivity. Diffusion is being shaped by cheap access, local constraints and thousands of small decisions about what is worth automating.

item.title: When geopolitics outruns the economics of supply chains — Lowy Institute
item.description:
Lowy Institute · September 14, 2026 · 4 min · Directly readable

G. Venkat Raman distinguishes three supply-chain strategies often collapsed into “decoupling.” Japanese firms are diversifying some production from China while retaining supplier depth and scale there. Chinese firms are moving production abroad but often bring supplier networks with them, forcing host governments to decide how much local value creation to demand. At the hardest national-security edge, firms may seek not merely non-China production but zero Chinese exposure anywhere in suppliers, personnel or equipment—a costly verification problem with no obvious endpoint.

Why it broadens: Treats de-risking as a spectrum with distinct economics. Moving a factory is easier than moving an ecosystem, and eliminating hidden dependencies can become more expensive than production itself.

item.title: 「只要燃煤在，就不怕缺電」 AI用電讓台灣脫不了煤，重啟核電有用嗎？ — 天下雜誌
item.description:
天下雜誌 CommonWealth · 2026年9月17日 · 約12分鐘 · 文章頁可直接讀取

劉光瑩從華亞汽電與和平電廠兩個相反案例，拆解台灣能源轉型的約束：前者因燃煤電力碳排過高而流失全球科技客戶，後者股東想退場，台電卻因北東電網基載需求不願放手。台灣2025年燃煤占比35.3%，未達原先30%的目標；經濟部估未來十年用電年增2.5%，約為過去十年的兩倍，AI與半導體投資、燃氣與電網建設延遲、地緣政治能源風險共同讓退煤更困難。

Why it broadens: 把能源轉型從「選哪種發電」改寫成供電可靠度、區域電網、企業減碳壓力、建設時程與需求成長的共同約束。政策口號不能同時消除所有取捨。
